# pretest 1.0.0

Pre-pentest self-assessment for web systems: one file, no dependencies, any host.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

Installs to `~/.local/bin/pretest`. Or take the file itself:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/pretest.py -o pretest
chmod +x pretest
sha256sum pretest.pretest.py  # see below
```

Verify the asset you downloaded:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/download/v1.0.0/pretest.py.sha256 | sha256sum -c -
```

## Use

```bash
pretest --url https://example.com
pretest --url https://example.com --domain example.com --repo ~/code/app
pretest --url https://app.example.com -H "Cookie: session=…"   # behind a login
pretest --url https://example.com --fail-on high               # CI gate
pretest --self-test                                            # verify the tool
```

## What it looks for

Exposed artefacts (`.git`, `.env`, dumps, actuator, pprof, source maps, swagger,
GraphQL), transport and TLS (redirect, HSTS, certificate, legacy protocols),
header hygiene, cookie flags, CORS reflection, SPF/DMARC/DKIM/CAA, subdomains via
crt.sh with dangling-CNAME takeover detection, 20 common ports, secrets in source,
and known dependency CVEs through `npm audit`/`pip-audit`/`cargo audit` when those
are installed.

Anything it could not check is reported as `info`. It never goes quiet.

## Limits

- Not a pentest: no IDOR, no business logic, no injections in your own parameters.
- Report text is Swedish; every finding has a stable English `id` in the JSON.
- TLS 1.0/1.1 are reported as *untested* on a modern OpenSSL, not as unsupported.
- Port findings behind a CDN describe the CDN edge, and say so.
- Linux and macOS are tested; Windows is not.
